## Personality

A notable figure in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), this woman is widely recognized for her capable, practical, and hardworking nature. She possesses an outspoken personality and prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor, though her critical and meddlesome tendencies frequently earn her a reputation as a notorious gossip. Enthusiastically opinionated, she is a red-hot politician, holds a strong prejudice against [Americans](../codex/factions.md#american), strongly opposes higher education for women, and is darkly dubious regarding the propriety of fiction. She compulsively seeks to correct and manage those around her, dearly loving to be asked for advice while continuously trying to bring others up properly. Beneath her sharp exterior lies a kind soul who never shirks her duties, proving herself to be a clever manager as well as a tender, patient, and gently skillful nurse when tending to her sick husband.

## History

Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/lynde.md), a longtime [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) resident who raised ten children, buried two, and knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts, lived as [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) Cuthbert's neighbor for forty-five years. She initially expressed strong disapproval when [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) and [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) decided to adopt an orphan, and she later engaged in a fierce argument with young [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) after insulting the girl's appearance, though she quickly accepted Anne's dramatic apology. Mrs. [Lynde](../character/lynde.md) frequently offered advice on community affairs, cautioning [Anne](../character/anne.md) against forming a Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvement-society) and later confirming that [Anne](../character/anne.md) had earned her students' respect after a necessary spanking at school. She actively tracked local events, investigating the unexpected arrival of Mr. Harrison's long-lost wife and keeping up with neighborhood news. Following the death of her husband, [Thomas](../character/thomas-lynde.md), [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) proposed that Mrs. [Lynde](../character/lynde.md) move into [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) so [Anne](../character/anne.md) could leave her teaching position to attend [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college). Residing at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) alongside [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and the orphaned twins, [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) and [Dora](../character/dora.md), Mrs. [Lynde](../character/lynde.md) maintained her role as a central source of local gossip. She kept [Anne](../character/anne.md) informed about community developments during her college breaks, including news of [Ruby](../character/ruby-gillis.md) Gillis's terminal illness and [Diana](../character/diana.md) Barry's upcoming marriage.

## Quotes

> "But really, Green Gables doesn’t seem as out of the world as it used to do . . . Anne has lots of company and the twins make it real lively. And anyhow, I’d rather live at the bottom of a well than leave Avonlea."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 XXVI Around the Bend P27](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0027)

> "and as for the twins, I’ll be glad to do all I can for them; but I won’t undertake to answer Davy’s questions, that’s what. I’m not an encyclopedia, neither am I a Philadelphia lawyer. You’ll miss Anne for that."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 XXVI Around the Bend P29](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0029)

> "I never saw her look so pleasant before, that’s what. Well, there weren’t many tears shed over her, poor old soul. The Elisha Wrights are thankful to be rid of her, and I can’t say I blame them a mite."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v3 ch.Evening P11](../source/v03-c28.md#nw-v03-c28-p0011)

> "She’s terrible skinny and homely, Marilla. Come here, child, and let me have a look at you. Lawful heart, did any one ever see such freckles? And hair as red as carrots! Come here, child, I say."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014)

> "I saw Mr. Harrison chasing your Jersey out of his oats today when I was coming home from Carmody. I thought he looked pretty mad. Did he make much of a rumpus?"
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 I An Irate Neighbor P38](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0038)

## Relationships

### [Anne](../character/anne.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne--rachel-lynde.md)

The relationship began with sharp hostility when Rachel Lynde insulted Anne's appearance, driving [Anne](../character/anne.md) into an explosive rage. However, after [Anne](../character/anne.md) offered a dramatic apology, Rachel completely forgave her and offered comforting words about her hair. Over time, Rachel evolved into a well-meaning neighbor and trusted advisor, frequently dropping by to offer counsel and share community news as [Anne](../character/anne.md) grew up.

- Enemy of — insulted Anne and faced intense mutual hostility  _(ended v1)_  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P16](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0016)</sub>
- Friend of — well-meaning older neighbour and advisor (since v2)  <sub>[v2 I An Irate Neighbor P54](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0054)</sub>

### [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Rachel and [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) maintain a longstanding, close neighborly friendship, regularly visiting one another to exchange local news and discuss household matters. Though Rachel initially expressed blunt disapproval over Marilla's plan to adopt an orphan, she remains a constant presence at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) routinely seeks Rachel's practical advice on raising and managing [Anne](../character/anne.md).

- Friend of — longstanding neighborly friendship  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P12](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0012), [v1 CHAPTER XV.
